info.name: Mangal Superfoods API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Mangal Superfoods backend (Express + Prisma/Postgres).

**Base URL:** `{{base_url}}` — defaults to `http://localhost:4000`. All resource routes are mounted under `/api`; `/health` is not.

**Authentication:** none. There is no session/token middleware — every route is unprotected at the HTTP layer. Role checks (ADMIN/SELLER) are enforced client-side in the frontend only, so "admin only" notes below are conventions, not enforcement.

**Sample data:** the variable defaults match `prisma/seed.mjs`. Run `npm run prisma:db:seed` first, and `npm run init:s3` before touching product image endpoints.

**Docs:** `docs/API_REFERENCE.md`, `docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md`.

request.description:
Authenticate with mobile + password. Passwords are stored as scrypt `salt:key`.

**Validation:** `mobile` must be exactly 10 digits; `password` non-empty.

**Errors:** `400` invalid mobile/password format · `404` user not found · `401` invalid credentials · `500` internal error.

request.description:
Register a new user.

**`id` is optional** — like every other model, `User.id` defaults to a uuid v4 generated by Prisma. The pre-request script still supplies a unique `id` (plus a unique `mobile`) so the request stays re-runnable and later requests can reference the created user.

**Required:** `name`.
**Optional:** `email`, `image`, `mobile` (10 digits, unique), `password` (hashed with scrypt), `cart` (JSON, defaults `{}`), `role` (`CUSTOMER` | `ADMIN` | `SELLER`, defaults `CUSTOMER`).

**Errors:** `400` missing `name` · `409` mobile already registered · `500` failed to create.

Update a user's `name` and/or `email`. The target user is identified by `id` **in the body** — there is no `/api/users/:id` route.

Only `name` and `email` are updatable here; `mobile`, `role`, `cart` and `password` are ignored.

**Errors:** `400` missing `id` · `404` user not found · `500` failed to update.

formdata.description: Optional. Only the exact string "false" turns it off; anything else is true.
Required — at least one file. Attach one or more images before sending.

request.description:
Create a product. **`multipart/form-data` only** — do not set a `Content-Type` header manually, Postman sets the boundary.

Files are uploaded to S3 first, then the resulting URLs (`{S3_ENDPOINT}/{BUCKET_NAME}/{timestamp}-{originalname}`) are stored on the `images` array. Run `npm run init:s3` so the bucket exists locally.

**Required:** `name`, `description`, `mrp`, `price`, `category`, and at least one `images` file.

**Errors:** `400` missing fields · `400` no images · `500` S3 upload failed · `500` failed to create.

> ⚠️ **Attach a file to `images` before sending** — with an empty file field the request returns `400 At least one image is required`.

formdata.description: Optional. Only the exact string "true" sets it true; anything else sets it false.
JSON array string of image URLs to KEEP. Omitting this wipes all existing images.
Optional — new files to append after existingImages

request.description:
Update a product. Every field is optional; only the ones you send are applied.

The final `images` array is `existingImages` (URLs you want to keep) **concatenated with** the newly uploaded files.

> ⚠️ **`existingImages` is destructive when omitted.** It defaults to `[]`, and the resulting empty array is still written to the row — so any PUT that leaves it out clears every image on the product. Always send the current image URLs you want to retain.

> ⚠️ **`inStock` is compared against the string `"true"`.** Send `"true"` / `"false"` as text. A JSON boolean `true` does **not** match and is stored as `false`.

**Errors:** `500` failed to update (including for a non-existent id — this route does not return `404`).

formdata.description: REQUIRED here — omit it and the product's images are erased

request.description:
Flip a product's in-stock flag. Same `PUT /api/products/:id` handler as the full edit — there is no dedicated stock endpoint.

Sent as form-data rather than JSON on purpose:

1. `inStock` is evaluated as `inStock === 'true'`, so it must be the **string** `"true"` or `"false"`. A JSON boolean `true` is stored as `false`.
2. `existingImages` must carry the product's current image URLs, otherwise the update writes an empty `images` array.

Fetch the product first (Get Product by ID) and paste its `images` into `existingImages` before sending.

Delete a product. Refused if the product appears in any `orderItems`.

**Success (200):** `{ "success": true }`

**Errors:** `404` product not found · `409` cannot delete product with existing orders · `500` failed to delete.

request.description:
Create an order and its `OrderItem` rows in a single nested Prisma create.

**Required:** `total` (non-zero number), `userId`, `addressId`, `paymentMethod` (`COD` | `STRIPE`), and a non-empty `orderItems` array of `{ productId, quantity, price }`.
**Optional:** `isCouponUsed` (defaults `false`), `coupon` (free-form JSON snapshot, defaults `{}`).

`status` always starts at `ORDER_PLACED` and `isPaid` at `false` — neither can be set at creation.

**Errors:** `400` missing required fields · `500` failed to create (this is also what you get for a bad `userId`/`addressId`/`productId`, since the FK violation is not mapped to a `404`).

> Note: `total` is checked with `!total`, so a `total` of `0` is rejected as a missing field.

Transition an order's status. This route updates **only** `status` — no other field is writable.

**Allowed values:** `ORDER_PLACED` → `PROCESSING` → `SHIPPED` → `DELIVERED`. Any other value is rejected; note the handler does not enforce ordering, so it will accept a backwards transition.

**Errors:** `400` status required · `400` invalid status · `500` failed to update (also returned for an unknown order id).

Fetch every address in the system, each with its `user` relation included.

There is no auth layer, so this is not scoped to a caller — use the `?userId=` variant for a single customer's address book.

request.description:
Submit a review for a product the user actually ordered.

**Required:** `rating`, `userId`, `productId`, **`orderId`**.
**Optional:** `review` (defaults to `''`).

> ⚠️ `rating` is parsed with `parseInt` and must land in **1–5**. Fractional values like `4.5` are truncated to `4`; `0` is rejected both by the range check and by the `!rating` guard.

`(userId, productId, orderId)` is unique — a second review for the same product in the same order returns `409`.

**Errors:** `400` missing required fields · `400` rating out of range · `404` product not found · `404` user not found · `409` already rated · `500` failed to create.

request.description:
Create a coupon (admin action).

**Required:** `code` (the primary key — there is no separate id), `description`, `discount` (0–100 percentage), `expiresAt` (ISO 8601 datetime).
**Optional:** `forNewUser`, `forMember`, `isPublic` — all default to `false`.

**Errors:** `400` missing required fields · `400` discount must be between 0 and 100 · `409` coupon code already exists · `500` failed to create.

Generate a 4-digit OTP and deliver it over WhatsApp via whapi.cloud.

The message body comes from the `OtpTemplate` row keyed `LOGIN_OTP`, which is auto-created on first use. The number is dialled as `91{mobile}` (India country code hardcoded), and the code is persisted to `OtpCode` with a **5-minute** expiry — but only *after* the provider accepts the send.

**Required:** `mobile`, exactly 10 digits.

**Errors:** `400` invalid mobile number · `500` `WHAPI_TOKEN` not configured · `502` SMS provider rejected the send · `500` internal error.

> This hits a real paid provider. Without `WHAPI_TOKEN` set you get a `500` and no OTP row is written — to test `/verify` locally, insert an `OtpCode` row directly (e.g. via `npm run prisma:studio`).

exec: pm.test('Body carries a success flag', function () {

request.description:
Check an OTP against the most recent matching, unused, unexpired `OtpCode` row and mark it used.

**Required:** `mobile` (10 digits), `otp` (4 digits). Set the `otp` collection variable to the code you actually received — there is no fixed test code.

Unlike the rest of the API, this endpoint's errors carry a `success: false` field alongside `error`.

**Errors (all `400` unless noted):** mobile and OTP are required · invalid mobile format · invalid OTP format · OTP invalid or expired · `500` internal error.

> Verification does not create a session or token — the frontend treats a `success: true` as proof and proceeds on its own.
